'''''Euthynnus affinis''''', the '''mackerel tuna''', '''little tuna''', '''eastern little tuna''', '''wavyback skipjack tuna''', '''kawakawa''',<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hooper |first1=Robin |editor1-last=Pawley |editor1-first=A.K. |editor2-last=Ross |editor2-first=M.D. |chapter=Reconstructing Proto Polynesian fish names |title=Austronesian terminologies: continuity and change |date=1994 |pages=223–4 |doi=10.15144/PL-C127.185 |publisher=Pacific Linguistics, Australian National University}}</ref> or '''tongkol komo''' is a [[species]] of [[ray-finned]] [[bony fish]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Scombridae]], or [[mackerel]] family. It belongs to the [[tribe (biology)|tribe]] [[Thunnini]], better known as the [[tuna]]s.<ref>{{ITIS|id=172403|taxon=''Euthynnus affinis''|access-date=2 November 2012}}</ref> It is also in the genus [[Euthynnus]] of "little tunas," which includes the [[little tunny]] and the [[Euthynnus lineatus|black skipjack]].

''Euthynnus affinis'' formerly was known as '''''Euthynnus yaito'''''.<ref>[http://www.marinespecies.org/aphia.php?p=taxdetails&id=304441] World Register of Marine Species ''Euthynnus yaito'' Kishinouye, 1915</ref>
